landmarks.name: Lost City Hydrothermal Field
landmarks.summary: A field of towering carbonate chimneys on the Atlantis Massif, venting warm alkaline fluid driven by serpentinization rather than magma, hosting unique microbial life relevant to origin-of-life research.
facts: Chimneys are carbonate, not sulfide, and among the tallest known vent structures (~60 m, 'Poseidon')
Powered by serpentinization of mantle rock, not magmatic heat
Discovered in December 2000 using DSV Alvin
Considered a model for possible life on icy moons like Enceladus
gameplay_hooks: Climb and sample the Poseidon carbonate tower
Compare alkaline vent chemistry to black smokers
Astrobiology research side-quest referencing icy moons

landmarks.name: TAG Hydrothermal Field
landmarks.summary: Trans-Atlantic Geotraverse (TAG) hydrothermal field, a classic black-smoker sulfide mound on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, studied since the 1980s and a model site for seafloor massive sulfide deposits.
facts: One of the best-studied black smoker sites, active for tens of thousands of years
Sulfide mound is roughly 200 m in diameter and 50 m tall
Drilled by ODP Leg 158 to study sub-seafloor sulfide structure
Fluids reach temperatures over 360 degrees C
gameplay_hooks: Core-drill the sulfide mound for mineral samples

landmarks.name: Rainbow Hydrothermal Field
landmarks.summary: An ultramafic-hosted hydrothermal field on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge near the Azores, producing metal-rich, highly acidic fluids from serpentinizing peridotite.
facts: Hosted in mantle peridotite rather than typical basalt
Fluids are notably rich in iron, hydrogen, and methane
Supports dense shrimp swarms similar to TAG and Snake Pit
Within the OSPAR Rainbow Hydrothermal Field Marine Protected Area
gameplay_hooks: Compare ultramafic vs basaltic vent chemistry

landmarks.name: Snake Pit Hydrothermal Field
landmarks.summary: A basalt-hosted black smoker field on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge south of the Kane Fracture Zone, named for its dense clusters of eel-like zoarcid fish and vent shrimp.
facts: Discovered in 1985 during Alvin dives
Named for dense aggregations of shrimp and fish resembling a pit of snakes
Classic basalt-hosted black smoker chemistry
gameplay_hooks: Black smoker chimney growth time-lapse mission

landmarks.name: Endeavour Hydrothermal Vents
landmarks.region: Juan de Fuca Ridge, NE Pacific
landmarks.summary: A cluster of large black-smoker sulfide edifices on the Juan de Fuca Ridge, designated Canada's first Marine Protected Area and monitored by the NEPTUNE/Ocean Networks Canada cabled observatory.
facts: Canada's first Marine Protected Area, designated 2003
Hosts massive sulfide structures including 'Godzilla' (since collapsed)
Continuously monitored via the Ocean Networks Canada NEPTUNE cabled array
Located on the fast-spreading Juan de Fuca Ridge
gameplay_hooks: Live-data tie-in with real-time seismic/vent sensors
Track chimney growth using NEPTUNE observatory feeds

landmarks.name: Axial Seamount / ASHES Vent Field
landmarks.region: Juan de Fuca Ridge, NE Pacific
landmarks.summary: The most active submarine volcano on the Juan de Fuca Ridge, hosting the ASHES vent field within its caldera; instrumented by the Ocean Observatories Initiative Regional Cabled Array for real-time eruption monitoring.
facts: Erupted in 1998, 2011, and 2015; monitored for future eruptions
Hosts the Ocean Observatories Initiative cabled array with real-time sensors
Summit caldera is roughly 3 by 8 km
ASHES vent field lies within the caldera's western wall
gameplay_hooks: Eruption-prediction mission using live seismic/pressure data
Caldera-floor exploration with lava-flow hazard timer

landmarks.name: Guaymas Basin Vent Field
landmarks.summary: A sediment-covered spreading center in the Gulf of California where hydrothermal fluids percolate through thick organic-rich sediment, producing oil-like hydrocarbons and unique microbial mats instead of bare-rock black smokers.
facts: Sediment-hosted vents create petroleum-like hydrocarbons via thermal alteration of organic matter
Home to thick white mats of the giant sulfur bacterium Beggiatoa
Studied extensively by Alvin and, in 2022, by DSV Limiting Factor and remote teams
Site of unusual 'methane ice worms' and abundant tubeworms
gameplay_hooks: Sample hydrocarbon seep chemistry vs vent chemistry

landmarks.name: Loki's Castle Vent Field
landmarks.summary: The northernmost known hydrothermal vent field at the time of its 2008 discovery, located at the junction of the Mohns and Knipovich ridges, named for its two paired sulfide mounds.
facts: Discovered in 2008 by University of Bergen researchers
Named after Norse mythology's Loki, referencing its castle-like twin sulfide towers
Hosted the discovery of the Lokiarchaeota, an archaeal lineage important to understanding eukaryote origins
Located at the boundary of the Mohns and Knipovich Ridges
gameplay_hooks: Archaea-sampling mission tied to Lokiarchaeota discovery lore
Arctic vent-field mapping under polar conditions

landmarks.name: Beebe Hydrothermal Vent Field (Piccard)
landmarks.summary: The deepest known active hydrothermal vent field on Earth, on the ultraslow-spreading Mid-Cayman Spreading Centre. Its black smokers release low-salinity fluid measured around 401–403 °C at roughly 500 bar.
facts: World's deepest known active hydrothermal vent field at ~4,960 m
Low-salinity fluids measured around 401–403 °C at roughly 500 bar can be supercritical (Webber et al. 2015)
Named after ocean explorer William Beebe
On the ultraslow-spreading Mid-Cayman Spreading Centre alongside the shallower Von Damm field

landmarks.name: Rose Garden / Galápagos Rift Vent Field
landmarks.summary: Site of the 1977 discovery of hydrothermal vents and chemosynthetic life on the Galápagos Rift, which overturned prior assumptions that life depended entirely on sunlight; the original 'Rose Garden' site has since gone dormant and was succeeded by 'Rosebud'.
facts: Site of the 1977 Alvin dive that discovered chemosynthesis-based ecosystems
Original Rose Garden vents went extinct by the 1990s after volcanic resurfacing
A successor field, 'Rosebud', later grew in nearly the same area
Giant tubeworms (Riftia pachyptila) were first described here
gameplay_hooks: Historical-discovery reenactment of the first vent-life find
Track ecosystem succession from Rose Garden to Rosebud

landmarks.name: East Pacific Rise 9°50'N Vent Field
landmarks.summary: One of the most intensively studied fast-spreading mid-ocean-ridge vent sites, monitored for decades to observe eruption cycles and rapid post-eruption ecological succession.
facts: Subject of long-term time-series studies since the 1980s (WHOI, Rutgers)
Experienced documented eruptions in 1991 and 2005-06 that reset local ecosystems
Fast-spreading ridge produces frequent volcanic resurfacing events
Key site for studying colonization and succession after eruptions

landmarks.name: Challenger Deep
landmarks.country_eez: Federated States of Micronesia / international (Mariana Trench)
landmarks.summary: The deepest known point in Earth's oceans, located in the southern Mariana Trench; consists of three en echelon basins with the eastern pool deepest.
facts: Deepest confirmed point on Earth's seafloor
First crewed descent 1960 (Trieste, Piccard & Walsh)
2019 Five Deeps Expedition surveyed three sub-basins
Pressure exceeds 1,000 atmospheres
Named after HMS Challenger, first sounded it in 1875
gameplay_hooks: Full-ocean-depth descent sequence with hull-stress mechanic
Locate and compare the three sub-basins
Deploy a lander to the eastern pool

landmarks.name: Sirena Deep
landmarks.summary: Third-deepest oceanic point on Earth, located in the Mariana Trench roughly 200 km east of Challenger Deep.
facts: First surveyed in detail by a Japanese sonar expedition in 1997
Depth estimates vary 10,666-10,714 m across surveys
Lies along the same subduction trench as Challenger Deep
gameplay_hooks: Comparative depth-survey mission against Challenger Deep
Sonar-mapping minigame to resolve conflicting depth readings

landmarks.name: Horizon Deep (Tonga Trench)
landmarks.summary: Second-deepest point on Earth and deepest in the Southern Hemisphere, in the Tonga Trench where the Pacific plate subducts fastest on the planet.
facts: Deepest point in the Southern Hemisphere
Subduction here is the fastest on Earth, ~24 cm/yr
Named for research vessel Horizon, which found it in 1952
Only ~105 m shallower than Challenger Deep

landmarks.name: Molloy Deep
landmarks.summary: Deepest point of the Arctic Ocean, located in the Molloy Hole/Fram Strait between Greenland and Svalbard on the Molloy Transform Fault.
facts: Deepest point in the entire Arctic Ocean
Sits on the Molloy Transform Fault linking the Knipovich and Lena Trough spreading ridges
Named after oceanographer Arthur Molloy
gameplay_hooks: Under-ice descent mission with sea-ice navigation puzzle
Compare Arctic vs. tropical trench ecosystems

landmarks.name: Milwaukee Deep (Puerto Rico Trench)
landmarks.summary: Deepest point in the Atlantic Ocean, located in the Puerto Rico Trench north of Puerto Rico.
facts: Deepest point in the Atlantic basin
Associated with the boundary between the Caribbean and North American plates
Region capable of generating tsunamis threatening the Caribbean

landmarks.name: Java Trench (Sunda Trench)
landmarks.summary: Deepest point in the Indian Ocean, formed where the Indo-Australian plate subducts beneath the Sunda plate; source region of the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake.
facts: Deepest point of the Indian Ocean
Segment that ruptured in the 2004 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake and tsunami
Also called the Sunda Trench

landmarks.name: Kuril-Kamchatka Trench
landmarks.summary: A deep subduction trench off the Kuril Islands and Kamchatka Peninsula, part of the Pacific Ring of Fire.
facts: One of the deepest trenches in the Pacific, exceeding 9,600 m
Formed by subduction of the Pacific plate beneath the Okhotsk plate
Highly seismically active, produces major earthquakes and tsunamis

landmarks.name: Atacama Trench (Peru-Chile Trench)
landmarks.summary: Deep subduction trench off the coast of Chile and Peru where the Nazca plate subducts beneath South America; site of dedicated hadal biology research (Atacama Trench expeditions).
facts: Deepest trench in the eastern Pacific
Target of the 2018 Atacama Trench hadal expedition (HADES)
Home to endemic hadal snailfish species

landmarks.name: Meteor Deep (South Sandwich Trench)
landmarks.country_eez: international (near South Sandwich Islands, UK claim)
landmarks.summary: Deepest point of the Southern Ocean, in the South Sandwich Trench where the South American plate subducts beneath the Sandwich microplate.
facts: Deepest point of the Southern Ocean
Named after German research vessel Meteor
Surveyed by the Five Deeps Expedition in 2019
gameplay_hooks: Southern Ocean depth-record dive amid strong currents and icebergs

landmarks.name: Kama'ehuakanaloa (Lo'ihi) Seamount
landmarks.summary: An active submarine shield volcano rising over 3,000 m from the seafloor southeast of the Big Island of Hawaii; the presumed next Hawaiian island in the making.
facts: Renamed from Lo'ihi to Kama'ehuakanaloa in 2021, honoring Hawaiian tradition
Summit lies about 975 m below sea level, could breach the surface in tens of thousands of years
Hosts active hydrothermal venting and iron-oxidizing microbial mats
Experienced a major seismic swarm and collapse event in 1996
gameplay_hooks: Watch a future-island-in-the-making volcanic vent field

landmarks.name: Davidson Seamount
landmarks.summary: A large extinct volcanic seamount off central California within Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary, renowned for dense deep-sea coral and sponge gardens.
facts: Rises about 2,400 m from the seafloor but its summit stays 1,250 m below the surface, never reaching shallow water
Protected as part of Monterey Bay National Marine Sanctuary
Hosts extensive gardens of bubblegum coral and other deep-sea corals
First surveyed in detail via ROV in the early 2000s

landmarks.name: Bowie Seamount
landmarks.summary: A shallow-summit seamount off the coast of British Columbia, designated as SGaan Kinghlas-Bowie Seamount Marine Protected Area, rich in productive upwelling-driven marine life.
facts: Summit is only about 24 m below the surface, unusually shallow for an offshore seamount
Protected as Canada's SGaan Kinghlas-Bowie Seamount Marine Protected Area since 2008
Name 'SGaan Kinghlas' means 'supernatural being looking outward' in Haida
Supports a highly productive food web due to upwelling around the peak

landmarks.name: Great Meteor Seamount
landmarks.summary: One of the largest guyots (flat-topped seamounts) in the Atlantic, rising over 4,000 m from the abyssal plain, an important biodiversity hotspot for pelagic and benthic species.
facts: A guyot with a flat summit formed by ancient wave erosion before subsiding
Rises roughly 4,000 m above the surrounding abyssal seafloor
Important feeding ground for seabirds, tuna, and marine mammals
Studied extensively by German research vessel Meteor, its namesake
gameplay_hooks: Flat-top guyot exploration and ancient shoreline forensic mission

landmarks.name: Vema Seamount
landmarks.summary: A remarkably shallow-summit seamount in the South Atlantic rising over 4,600 m from the abyssal plain, discovered by the research vessel Vema in 1959.
facts: Summit lies only about 26 m below the surface
Rises more than 4,600 m from the surrounding seafloor, comparable in height to major mountains
Hosts kelp and rock lobster despite its remote mid-ocean location
Named after the research vessel Vema that discovered it in 1959
gameplay_hooks: Mid-ocean shallow-reef 'oasis' exploration far from any coastline

landmarks.name: Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha’apai (pre-2022 survey)
landmarks.summary: Explore the earlier summit landscape of Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha’apai, before the January 2022 eruption deepened its shallow caldera to about 850 m.
facts: The January 2022 eruption sent a plume about 58 km high and generated a destructive tsunami
Caldera floor deepened from roughly 150 m to about 850 m after the eruption
Caldera widened to about 4 km across
Generated a Pacific-wide tsunami and unprecedented atmospheric shockwaves
hazards: dim water on the deeper flank

landmarks.name: Kick 'em Jenny
landmarks.summary: The Caribbean's most active submarine volcano, located about 8 km north of Grenada, which has erupted more than a dozen times since its first recorded eruption in 1939.
facts: Most active submarine volcano in the Caribbean, with 12+ recorded eruptions since 1939
Summit lies about 180 m below sea level and continues to grow
Monitored by the University of the West Indies Seismic Research Centre
A shipping exclusion zone is enforced around it during unrest

landmarks.name: Havre Seamount
landmarks.summary: A submarine volcano on the Kermadec Arc that produced the largest deep-ocean silicic eruption ever documented in 2012, creating a vast raft of floating pumice.
facts: 2012 eruption created a pumice raft covering over 400 sq km of ocean surface
Largest known deep-sea silicic (rhyolite) eruption ever recorded/surveyed
Studied in detail via post-eruption ROV mapping expeditions
Part of the highly active Kermadec volcanic arc
gameplay_hooks: Pumice-raft tracking and eruption-deposit mapping mission

landmarks.name: Tamu Massif
landmarks.summary: The largest single volcano yet identified on Earth, forming the bulk of the Shatsky Rise plateau about 1,600 km east of Japan; an extinct shield volcano roughly the size of the British Isles.
facts: Largest known single shield volcano on Earth by area, comparable to the size of New Mexico
Summit lies about 1,980 m deep; base extends to roughly 6.4 km depth
Formed about 145 million years ago near a triple junction of tectonic plates
Named after Texas A&M University, whose researchers helped identify it

landmarks.name: Monterey Canyon
landmarks.summary: The largest submarine canyon on the US West Coast, comparable in scale to the Grand Canyon, extending from Moss Landing beach out to abyssal depths in Monterey Bay.
facts: Comparable in size and depth to the Grand Canyon
Reaches depths of over 3,600 m within roughly 100 km of the shoreline
Intensively studied by MBARI using ROVs and cabled observatories
Hosts frequent turbidity-current sediment flows that reshape the canyon floor
gameplay_hooks: Follow a simulated turbidity current down-canyon

landmarks.name: Hudson Canyon
landmarks.summary: The largest submarine canyon off the US East Coast, an offshore extension of the ancient Hudson River channel; NOAA has proposed it as a National Marine Sanctuary.
facts: Largest submarine canyon on the US Atlantic seaboard
Formed as an extension of the Hudson River during past glacial low sea-level periods
Proposed as Hudson Canyon National Marine Sanctuary (NOAA, 2022); not yet designated
Supports deep-sea coral communities and important fish spawning habitat
gameplay_hooks: Trace the ancient drowned river channel from shelf to abyss

landmarks.name: Zhemchug Canyon
landmarks.summary: The largest submarine canyon in the world by volume and cross-sectional area, cutting into the edge of the Bering Sea continental shelf.
facts: Largest submarine canyon on Earth by volume (~5,800 cubic km) and area
Vertical relief of about 2,600 m, deeper than the Grand Canyon
Important habitat for pollock and other commercially vital fish stocks
Named after the Russian research vessel Zhemchug
gameplay_hooks: Fisheries/ecosystem survey along the shelf break

landmarks.name: Congo Canyon
landmarks.country_eez: Angola / Democratic Republic of the Congo
landmarks.summary: One of the largest submarine canyons in the world, a direct continuation of the Congo River that channels sediment and organic debris far into the deep Atlantic.
facts: Extends over 800 km from the Congo River mouth into the deep Atlantic
One of only a few submarine canyons connected directly to a major river without an intervening delta plain
Hosts periodic dense turbidity-current flows that can snap seafloor cables
Nutrient input supports distinct deep-sea faunal communities
gameplay_hooks: Trace terrestrial river sediment into the deep sea

landmarks.name: Nazaré Canyon
landmarks.summary: One of the largest submarine canyons in Europe, funneling deep swells that make Nazaré, Portugal famous for record-breaking big-wave surfing at the surface above.
facts: Canyon's underwater topography focuses ocean swell energy, producing some of the largest surfable waves on Earth at Nazaré
Extends over 200 km and reaches depths near 5,000 m
Hosts cold-water coral habitats along its steep flanks
Studied for both geohazard (turbidity current) and biological interest
gameplay_hooks: Wave-focusing physics tie-in with famous surf break above
Cold-water coral wall exploration on canyon flanks

landmarks.name: Whittard Canyon
landmarks.summary: A branching submarine canyon system on the Celtic Sea continental margin known for extensive cold-water coral gardens and unusual seafloor chemosynthetic communities near canyon-head landslides.
facts: Complex branching, multi-headed canyon system cutting the Celtic margin
Hosts extensive Lophelia and Madrepora cold-water coral gardens
Canyon heads have exposed methane-related authigenic carbonate and chemosynthetic fauna
Studied extensively by UK and Irish marine research cruises
gameplay_hooks: Chemosynthetic seep discovery within a canyon head

landmarks.name: Perth Canyon
landmarks.summary: A large submarine canyon off Western Australia comparable in scale to the Grand Canyon, an important feeding ground for pygmy blue whales.
facts: Comparable in scale to the Grand Canyon in both depth and length
Seasonal upwelling within the canyon draws krill swarms and feeding pygmy blue whales
Located within the Perth Canyon Marine Park
Cuts across the edge of the Australian continental shelf

landmarks.name: Mid-Atlantic Ridge near Azores (Lucky Strike)
landmarks.summary: A segment of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge near the Azores hosting the well-studied Lucky Strike hydrothermal vent field atop a large volcanic lava lake structure, monitored by the EMSO-Azores cabled observatory.
facts: Home to the Lucky Strike vent field, sited over a large sub-seafloor magma lake
Monitored continuously by the EMSO-Azores deep-sea observatory
One of the most-visited vent sites for scientific research due to proximity to the Azores
Hosts dense mussel beds distinct from Pacific vent fauna

landmarks.name: Juan de Fuca Ridge
landmarks.summary: A mid-ocean spreading ridge off the Pacific Northwest coast, one of the most heavily instrumented seafloor regions on Earth via the NEPTUNE and Ocean Observatories Initiative cabled networks.
facts: Spreads at an intermediate rate, generating frequent volcanic and hydrothermal activity
Hosts both the Endeavour vent field and Axial Seamount
One of the most densely cabled and monitored stretches of seafloor on Earth
Subducts beneath North America at the nearby Cascadia subduction zone
gameplay_hooks: Regional overview mission linking Axial Seamount and Endeavour vents

landmarks.name: Bermuda Rise
landmarks.summary: A broad topographic swell of the Atlantic seafloor around Bermuda, thought to be a mantle hotspot-related uplift, with the volcanic Bermuda Pedestal rising near its center.
facts: A broad regional seafloor swell roughly 1,000 km across
Believed to result from a mantle hotspot beneath the Atlantic seafloor
Bermuda itself sits atop a small volcanic peak (the Bermuda Pedestal) on the rise
Region associated with the popular 'Bermuda Triangle' folklore
gameplay_hooks: Explore the Bermuda Pedestal volcanic core beneath the island

landmarks.name: Blake Plateau Coral Mound Province
landmarks.summary: The largest known deep-sea coral reef province on Earth, an expanse of thousands of Lophelia coral mounds spanning roughly the area of Florida beneath the Gulf Stream off the southeastern US.
facts: Announced by NOAA in 2024 as the largest deep-sea coral reef habitat yet mapped, roughly 500 km long
Comprises thousands of individual coral mounds up to tens of meters tall
Sits beneath the Gulf Stream at depths of roughly 200-1,000 m
Provides critical deep-sea fish and invertebrate habitat despite total darkness
gameplay_hooks: Vast coral-mound-field exploration and mapping mission

landmarks.name: Dean's Blue Hole
landmarks.summary: The world's deepest known ocean blue hole accessible from a beach, a near-vertical flooded sinkhole on Long Island, Bahamas, popular for competitive freediving.
facts: Depth of about 202 m, among the deepest blue holes on Earth
Opens directly from a sandy beach into a nearly vertical shaft
Hosts the annual Vertical Blue freediving competition
Widens dramatically into a large cavern below about 20 m depth
gameplay_hooks: Cavern-widening navigation puzzle below the entrance

landmarks.name: Lighthouse Reef / Great Blue Hole
landmarks.summary: Survey Lighthouse Reef’s shallow platform and outer slopes around the Great Blue Hole, a roughly 320 m-wide, 125 m-deep flooded limestone sinkhole in the Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System.
facts: The real sinkhole is about 320 m across and 125 m deep
Formed as a limestone cave system during Pleistocene low sea levels, then collapsed and flooded
Popularized by Jacques Cousteau's 1971 expedition
Part of the Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System UNESCO World Heritage Site
gameplay_hooks: Explore ancient stalactite formations proving past dry-cave origin

landmarks.name: Orca Basin Brine Pool ('Jacuzzi of Despair')
landmarks.summary: A vast pool of super-saline brine sitting in a seafloor depression in the Gulf of Mexico, so dense it forms a distinct underwater 'lake' with its own shoreline, toxic to most marine life that enters it.
facts: Brine is roughly 4-5 times saltier than normal seawater, creating a visible underwater lake surface
Toxic and low-oxygen, preserving carcasses of animals that wander in ('pickled' remains found at its edges)
Surrounded by chemosynthetic mussel beds fed by methane and sulfide seepage
Named for the nearby killer-whale-shaped seafloor contour
gameplay_hooks: Navigate the eerie underwater 'lake' shoreline without entering toxic brine
Chemosynthetic mussel-bed sampling at the pool's edge

landmarks.name: Cape Hatteras Methane Seeps
landmarks.summary: A cluster of active methane cold seeps discovered along the US Atlantic margin near Cape Hatteras, part of hundreds of newly identified seeps along the eastern seaboard.
facts: Part of a broader field of 500+ methane seeps discovered along the US Atlantic margin since 2012
Supports chemosynthetic mussel and tubeworm communities fueled by seeping methane
Methane bubble plumes ('flares') detectable via ship sonar
Seeps are linked to destabilizing methane hydrate deposits in the sediment
gameplay_hooks: Chemosynthetic community discovery mission distinct from hydrothermal vents

landmarks.name: Diamantina Fracture Zone
landmarks.summary: A deep transform fault scar in the Indian Ocean south of Australia, containing some of the deepest points in the Indian Ocean basin outside the Java Trench, notably searched during the MH370 investigation.
facts: Contains the Diamantina Deep and Dordrecht Deep, among the deepest points of the Indian Ocean
Searched extensively during the 2014-2017 hunt for missing flight MH370
Formed as a transform fault scarring the ocean floor as Australia and Antarctica separated
Rugged terrain with escarpments over 6 km deep
hazards: extremely rugged and largely unmapped terrain

landmarks.name: Chicxulub Crater Offshore Rim
landmarks.summary: The partially offshore rim of the Chicxulub impact crater, formed by the asteroid strike 66 million years ago linked to the end-Cretaceous mass extinction; much of the ring lies beneath the Gulf of Mexico continental shelf.
facts: Crater is roughly 180 km in diameter, straddling the Yucatán coastline and the Gulf of Mexico shelf
Formed by an asteroid impact ~66 million years ago implicated in the extinction of non-avian dinosaurs
The 'cenote ring' of sinkholes onshore traces the buried crater rim
IODP Expedition 364 drilled the offshore peak ring in 2016
gameplay_hooks: Drill-core geology mission tracing the extinction-event impact layer
Trace the submerged crater rim toward the onshore cenote ring

landmarks.name: Lomonosov Ridge
landmarks.country_eez: international waters (disputed extended-shelf claims: Russia, Canada, Denmark)
landmarks.summary: A submerged continental ridge spanning nearly the entire Arctic Ocean between Siberia and Ellesmere Island, at the center of overlapping extended-continental-shelf claims by Russia, Canada, and Denmark.
facts: Stretches roughly 1,800 km across the Arctic Ocean near the North Pole
Subject of competing UN continental-shelf claims by Russia, Canada, and Denmark/Greenland
A 2007 Russian expedition planted a titanium flag on the seabed at the North Pole nearby
Rises roughly 3,000 m above the adjacent Arctic basin floor
gameplay_hooks: Under-ice traverse toward the North Pole along the ridge crest

landmarks.name: Thwaites Glacier Grounding Zone
landmarks.summary: The submerged zone where the rapidly retreating Thwaites Glacier ('Doomsday Glacier') meets the seafloor in the Amundsen Sea, a critical site for understanding future sea-level rise; exact grounding-line position shifts yearly and is only approximated here.
facts: Thwaites Glacier alone could raise global sea level by over 60 cm if fully lost
Warm Circumpolar Deep Water intruding beneath the ice shelf is accelerating melt
The International Thwaites Glacier Collaboration deployed the Icefin ROV beneath the ice in 2019-2020
Grounding line has retreated several kilometers in recent decades, so its precise position is a moving target, hence low confidence here
gameplay_hooks: Under-ice-shelf ROV mission (Icefin-style) mapping the grounding line
Climate-science time-pressure narrative: document retreat before it's gone

landmarks.name: Chatham Rise (Zealandia)
landmarks.region: South Pacific, east of New Zealand
landmarks.summary: A broad, relatively shallow submerged plateau east of New Zealand, part of the largely submerged continent of Zealandia, roughly 94% of which lies underwater.
facts: Part of Zealandia, a nearly 5 million sq km submerged continent, ~94% underwater
Chatham Rise supports one of New Zealand's most productive fisheries
Zealandia separated from Gondwana roughly 80 million years ago and subsided beneath the waves
Confirmed as a distinct continent by geologists in 2017
gameplay_hooks: Sunken-continent exploration narrative highlighting Zealandia's discovery

landmarks.name: Røst Reef
landmarks.summary: The world's largest known cold-water coral reef, discovered in 2002 off the Lofoten Islands, Norway, stretching over 40 km and built by the coral Lophelia pertusa.
facts: Largest known cold-water Lophelia coral reef on Earth, roughly 40 x 3 km
Discovered in 2002 during Norwegian mapping surveys (MAREANO program)
Lies within an important cod-spawning ground, prompting fishing restrictions
Coral framework has built up over thousands of years in near-freezing water
gameplay_hooks: Vast cold-water reef traverse in near-freezing Nordic waters

landmarks.name: Darwin Mounds
landmarks.summary: A field of hundreds of sand-and-coral mounds northwest of Scotland, discovered in 1998, notable for cold-water Lophelia coral colonizing sediment mounds shaped by underlying gas escape structures, and for pioneering EU trawling bans that protect it.
facts: Discovered in 1998 during UK continental shelf mapping surveys
Mounds are built on sediment structures linked to ancient gas/fluid escape from below
Protected in 2003 by an emergency EU trawling ban, an early precedent for deep-sea habitat protection
Home to distinctive xenophyophore (giant single-celled organism) aggregations
hazards: historic trawling damage in unprotected areas

landmarks.name: Great Barrier Reef Outer Slope (Ribbon Reefs)
landmarks.summary: The outer drop-off of the world's largest coral reef system, where the shallow reef flat plunges into the Coral Sea, a globally iconic biodiversity showcase.
facts: World's largest coral reef system, visible from space, spanning over 2,300 km
Outer 'Ribbon Reefs' drop steeply from shallow reef flats into deep Coral Sea water
Home to over 1,500 fish species and 400 coral species
Severely impacted by repeated mass coral bleaching events since 2016
gameplay_hooks: Shallow-to-deep drop-off wall dive showcasing biodiversity

landmarks.name: Molokini Crater
landmarks.summary: A partially submerged volcanic crescent-shaped crater between Maui and Kaho'olawe, Hawaii, whose sheltered inner cove and outer back-wall drop-off make it a premier shallow snorkeling and diving showcase.
facts: A crescent-shaped tuff cone, remnant of a volcanic crater rim
Protected as a Hawaii State Marine Life Conservation District and seabird sanctuary
Back wall on the ocean side drops steeply from the surface to over 100 m
Exceptionally clear water due to lack of nearby freshwater runoff
gameplay_hooks: Sheltered-cove beginner showcase dive vs dramatic back-wall drop-off
hazards: strong currents on the outer back wall

landmarks.name: Silfra Fissure
landmarks.summary: A water-filled fissure in Þingvellir National Park, Iceland, formed along the divergent boundary between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, uniquely accessible as a dive/snorkel site where the mid-ocean ridge reaches the surface.
facts: One of very few places where the Mid-Atlantic Ridge rift is directly accessible to divers on land
Filled with glacial meltwater filtered through lava rock, giving over 100 m of visibility
Water temperature stays near 2-4 degrees C year-round
Fissure continues to widen a few centimeters per year as the plates diverge
gameplay_hooks: Touch-both-tectonic-plates showcase swim (North America and Europe)

landmarks.name: RMS Titanic
landmarks.summary: The famous ocean liner that sank on 15 April 1912 after striking an iceberg; the wreck was found by Robert Ballard's expedition in 1985 and lies in two main pieces about 600 m apart.
facts: Discovered September 1, 1985 by Robert Ballard/Jean-Louis Michel
Bow and stern sections lie ~600 m apart with a debris field between
Protected by the RMS Titanic international agreement, in force since November 2019
The 2023 Titan submersible implosion occurred during a dive to this wreck

Hood Association's 2001 expedition fix ('vicinity of 4809N 01607W'), ~20 km south of the old point; corroborated by a third published figure (48°09'N 016°07'W) distinct from Wikipedia's rounded infobox coordinate (48°10'N 16°12'W). See data/landmarks/bismarck/sources.md for the full discrepancy writeup. A seamount at the tile's southern edge matches accounts of the hull sliding down a slope.
